﻿Amended and Restated Shareholder Agreement
Effective Date: January 1, 2019
Recitals
WHEREAS, Summit Filing Solutions, Inc. (the “Company”) was incorporated in the State of Delaware on January 10, 2018;
WHEREAS, the Company elected to be treated as an S-Corporation under Subchapter S of the Internal Revenue Code, effective January 1, 2019;
WHEREAS, the shareholders desire to amend and restate the Shareholder Agreement with additional covenants and protections;
Article II – Subchapter S Election Matters
2.1 Maintenance of S‑Corporation Status. Shareholders shall take all actions necessary to maintain the Company's S‑Corporation status.
2.2 Tax Year. The tax year of the Company shall begin on January 1 of each year.
2.3 Pro Rata Distributions. All distributions shall be made strictly pro rata in accordance with share ownership to comply with the single‑class‑of‑stock rule.
2.4 Tax Distributions. The Company shall make quarterly tax distributions reflecting the highest blended marginal rate applicable to S‑Corp shareholders.
2.5 Mandatory Ordering. Distributions shall be applied (a) first to tax obligations, (b) second to shareholder loan repayments, (c) third to discretionary distributions.
Article III – Additional Covenants
3.1 Confidentiality. Shareholders shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding all Company information.
3.2 Non‑Competition. Except with Board consent, Shareholders shall not engage in any business that directly competes with the Company.
3.3 Non‑Solicitation. Shareholders shall not solicit the Company’s employees, contractors, or customers for two (2) years following any transfer of shares.
Article IV – Transfer Restrictions; Drag‑Along and Tag‑Along Rights
4.1 No Transfers to Ineligible Shareholders. No Shareholder may transfer shares to an individual or entity that would terminate S‑Corporation status.
4.2 Right of First Refusal. Before transferring any shares, the transferring Shareholder must first offer them to the Company and then to other Shareholders.
4.3 Tag‑Along Rights. If Shareholders holding at least 51% of the outstanding shares receive a bona fide offer from a third‑party purchaser, all minority Shareholders shall have the right to participate on the same terms and conditions.
4.4 Drag‑Along Rights. If Shareholders holding at least 75% of the outstanding shares approve a sale of the Company, all remaining Shareholders must consent and sell their shares on identical terms.
Article V – Board Governance and Procedures
5.1 Board Composition. The Board shall consist of three (3) directors unless amended by unanimous Shareholder consent.
5.2 Meetings. Regular meetings shall occur quarterly. Special meetings may be called by any director upon five (5) business days’ notice.
5.3 Voting. Board actions require a majority vote unless this Agreement specifies otherwise. Tax distributions and amendments to distribution methodology require unanimous Board approval.
5.4 Minutes. Written minutes shall be maintained and approved at the subsequent meeting.
Article VI – Dispute Resolution
6.1 Good Faith Negotiations. In the event of a dispute, the parties shall first attempt good‑faith negotiations for at least 30 days.
6.2 Mediation. If negotiations fail, the parties shall participate in confidential mediation administered by the American Arbitration Association (“AAA”).
6.3 Binding Arbitration. If mediation fails, disputes shall be resolved through binding arbitration under AAA Commercial Rules. Arbitration shall occur in the county of the Company’s principal place of business.
